signals_detected: EHR migration announced (Cerner or MEDITECH to Epic); Hiring interoperability or integration engineers; Account engagement spike
crm_context: Open opportunity, Ravid, stage unchanged for 41 days. Two contacts on the record, both in IT. Three visits to the integration docs page in the last week, all from the CIO's office.
why_now: A funded platform migration with a board deadline, four open integration requisitions, and docs traffic from the buyer's own team in the same week. Integration requirements for the target state are being written right now - after they are frozen, this becomes a change request.
recommended_action: Get into the EHR Transformation Program review, not the IT evaluation. Offer a target-state referral-data design against the migration plan, dated to their go-live.
channel: Exec intro via CIO, then programme review
what_would_change_it: If the migration is still 'evaluating vendors' rather than scheduled, this drops to Medium and the requirements window has not opened yet.

signals_detected: Health system acquires a provider group or hospital; Referral leakage or network integrity programme launched; New VP or Chief of Population Health / VBC
crm_context: Open opportunity, Ravid. Ridgeline Community Health sat in HubSpot as an unrelated parent account with its own owner until the hierarchy pass reparented it.
why_now: They closed an acquisition that added 720 providers on MEDITECH to an Epic system, then posted a referral-management role naming leakage explicitly. The integration office exists, is funded, and has a deadline. This is the cleanest why-now in the universe.
recommended_action: One conversation covering both entities. Lead with the merged referral process, which is running on spreadsheets, and show the hierarchy resolution as the artefact - their own CRM does not know these two are one company.
channel: Champion-led, warm via the integration office
what_would_change_it: If the acquisition has announced but not closed state review, the integration budget is not released yet and the timeline slips a quarter or two.

signals_detected: Payer enters a new state or files new MA counties; Prior-authorization automation initiative (CMS-0057); Provider directory accuracy or No Surprises Act exposure
crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl, largest open deal in the book. Six committee seats, one in HubSpot.
why_now: New MA county filings mean an adequate network has to be built to a regulatory date, while a CMS-0057 programme is already staffed against the same provider data. Two deadlines, one data problem, and a directory finding on the record that gives it an executive sponsor.
recommended_action: Reframe from an IT purchase to network adequacy. Bring Network Management in as co-buyer - the budget is larger there than in IT, and the deadline is theirs.
channel: Multithread: CIO plus SVP Network Management
what_would_change_it: If the county filings were withdrawn, the deadline disappears and this is an ordinary prior-auth conversation.

signals_detected: New value-based or full-risk contract with a payer; Payer-provider partnership or joint venture announced; Hiring interoperability or integration engineers
crm_context: Open opportunity, Ravid. Largest account in the universe. Contracts with four other Tier 1 accounts in this same table.
why_now: New risk arrangements with two systems already in the universe, and six open integration requisitions. The build-versus-buy decision is live, and the VP of Product would rather build.
recommended_action: Answer build-versus-buy in the first meeting, in writing, or Product becomes the blocker. The proof point is the relationship graph: four Tier 1 systems here are already their counterparties.
channel: VBC-led, with Product in the room from the start
what_would_change_it: If the integration requisitions are agency reposts rather than new headcount, build-versus-buy is not actually open and there is no urgency.

signals_detected: Epic Community Connect expansion to affiliates; New CIO or CDIO appointed; Account engagement spike
crm_context: Open opportunity, Ravid. The physicians network sits in HubSpot as its own record on a different domain; only the hierarchy pass links it to the parent.
why_now: A new Chief Digital & Information Officer in month four, inheriting a Cerner system and an acquired athenahealth group, and a Community Connect rollout that pushes one instance across organizations that do not share an owner. New CIOs are measured on visible convergence wins.
recommended_action: Lead with the two-EHR gap between the parent and the acquired group. That is a problem the new CIO was hired to solve and that Community Connect does not fix on its own.
what_would_change_it: If the CDIO is an internal promotion rather than an outside hire, the vendor reset does not happen and the existing roadmap holds.

signals_detected: New value-based or full-risk contract with a payer; Referral leakage or network integrity programme launched
crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl. Short evaluation cycles on record from the last two deals.
why_now: Full risk on 220k delegated lives across 1,900 providers they do not employ. Leakage is a direct P&L line, and a network-performance programme is already staffed against it.
recommended_action: Go straight at unit economics with the CMO: cost per leaked referral against 220k delegated lives. Expect the analytics director to benchmark against building it in-house.
what_would_change_it: If the new risk contract is a renewal rather than an expansion, the economics have not changed and this is a renewal-cycle conversation instead.

signals_detected: ACO REACH / MSSP participation change; Digital front door / patient access programme; Account engagement spike
crm_context: Open opportunity, Ravid. Previous cycle lost to 'we'll do it in Epic'. That objection is still on the record and unanswered.
why_now: They moved up a risk track, which puts downside exposure on the Chief Population Health Officer. Her budget moves faster than IT's, and the ACO is a separate legal entity with its own leadership - a path around the Epic objection rather than through it.
recommended_action: Route through Harborview ACO LLC and the population-health budget. Answer the Epic question in writing before the applications director asks it, because he will.
channel: Population-health budget, ACO entity as the vehicle
what_would_change_it: If the REACH change is a within-model track change rather than a new risk position, the economics did not move and the Epic objection stands.

signals_detected: Provider directory accuracy or No Surprises Act exposure; Prior-authorization automation initiative (CMS-0057)
crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl. Sibling of the provider parent, which is also an open opportunity with a different owner.
why_now: A directory finding plus a prior-auth programme on the same provider file. The unusual part is structural: the payer and the provider network share an ultimate parent, so the same executive owns both sides of the referral.
recommended_action: Sell the family, not the entity. One conversation with the system parent covering both the plan and the provider arm - and coordinate with the provider-side owner before either call.
channel: Coordinated with the provider-side account owner
what_would_change_it: If the directory finding was an industry-wide CMS sweep naming dozens of plans, it is not specific to them and the sponsor does not exist.

signals_detected: ACO REACH / MSSP participation change; Payer enters a new state or files new MA counties
crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl. Parent is the largest open deal in the book, under the same owner.
why_now: Delegated-risk contracts with Gulf Coast and Great Lakes - both in this universe - and Stars performance depends on care gaps closing, which depends on referrals landing. Separate P&L from the parent, so it can buy on its own timeline.
recommended_action: Sequence behind the parent rather than beside it. Use the parent conversation to earn the introduction, then run a separate cycle on the Stars economics.
what_would_change_it: If the parent deal stalls, this one is better run independently - the separate P&L is what makes that possible.

signals_detected: Account engagement spike; Stalled after engagement
crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl, no activity in 63 days. Two contacts, both marketing-sourced. Engagement in the last fortnight came from a resident, not from the committee.
why_now: Nothing external changed. The only movement is engagement from someone with no role in the decision, which the agent weights down rather than up.
what_would_change_it: This becomes real on any of: a new VBC or population-health hire, a risk contract with Meridian or Pinnacle, or engagement from the CIO or CMIO seat. All three are monitored.

crm_context: Open opportunity, Daryl, last activity 38 days ago. Four committee seats, none in HubSpot.
why_now: Just over the Tier 1 line on structure - Epic, 2,450 providers, a captive plan taking full MA risk - but no external signal has fired. Good account, wrong week.
channel: Nurture only; hold for a signal
what_would_change_it: A full-risk contract expansion at the captive plan, or a VBC hire, would move this to the top of the queue. Until then, forcing a touch spends the account.
